ProactiveConfig.description:
Alert policies (PRD §16): `[proactive]` in the user config file.

```toml
[proactive]
reserve_gib = 10          # "full" means less free space than this
alert_days = 14           # alert when a drive is forecast to be full within this
stale_worktree = "14d"    # worktrees idle for longer than this
stale_build = "30d"       # build outputs of projects idle for longer than this
stale_cache = "90d"       # caches untouched for longer than this
spike_gib = 20            # alert when something grows by this much...
spike_window = "24h"      # ...within this window
spike_percent = 50        # or by this percentage (and at least spike_min_gib); 0 = off
spike_min_gib = 5

[[proactive.budgets]]     # "all Rust target/ <= 50 GB"
category = "project_artifact"
ecosystem = "rust"
max_gib = 50

[[proactive.budgets]]     # "this project <= 30 GB"
path = "~/Projects/monorepo"
max_gib = 30
```

alert_days.description: Alert when a drive is forecast to drop below the reserve within this many days.

budgets.description: Size caps per category, ecosystem or path (PRO-03). None by default.

reserve_gib.description: "Full" means less free space than this many GiB (PRO-01).

spike_gib.description: Alert when a category or drive grows by this many GiB within `spike_window` (PRO-04).

spike_min_gib.description: ...when the growth is at least this many GiB.

spike_percent.description: Also alert on growth by this percentage within the window (0 turns it off)...

spike_window.description: The window spikes are measured over.

stale_build.description: Build outputs of projects idle for longer than this are stale (PRO-02).

stale_cache.description: Caches untouched for longer than this are stale (PRO-02).

stale_worktree.description: Worktrees idle for longer than this are stale (PRO-02).

QuarantineConfig.description:
Where the quarantine lives (P2-EXEC-13; PRD §10.6, D-3).

By default the quarantine of a volume is `<base>/.scull-quarantine/`, where `<base>` is
chosen automatically: the shallowest directory above the item, on its volume, that the
current user owns (usually the home directory). These settings replace that choice:

```toml
[quarantine]
base = "~/.scull-q"                       # for items on the volume holding this directory

[quarantine.bases]                        # per volume: longest matching prefix wins
"/Volumes/Data" = "/Volumes/Data/me/.q"
"D:\\" = "D:\\Users\\me\\q"
```

* For an item, the entry of `bases` whose key is the longest path prefix of the item's path
  applies; otherwise `base`; otherwise the automatic choice.
* A configured base must be on the **same volume** as the item. If it isn't, that item is
  not quarantined there: it falls back to the Trash (when enabled), else it is blocked. It
  is never moved across volumes and never deleted instead.
* The base is created owner-only (`0700` / protected DACL) when missing, must be a real
  directory (not a link) and must not be inside an item being cleaned; the
  `.scull-quarantine` folder inside it is created and checked owner-only.
* Repository files (`.scull.toml`) can't set these (CFG-03).

base.description: Directory that holds `.scull-quarantine` for items on its volume. `None`: automatic.

bases.description: Per volume (or any directory): items under the key use the value as their base.

activity_window.description: Items modified within this window are bumped one tier (default 24 h, D-8).

exclude.description: Paths never scanned (and so never candidates).

low_resource.description: Low-resource mode: fewer threads and lower I/O priority.

min_tier.description: Minimum tier for everything inside a path (e.g. `"~/Projects/legacy" = "S2"`).

protect.description: Protected paths: everything inside is S3 (PRD §8.3).

roots.description: Directories to scan. Empty by default: roots must be explicit (CFG-04).

oneOf.description: Powers of 1024 (KiB, MiB, GiB).
Powers of 1000 (kB, MB, GB).

Tier.description:
How much risk removing an item carries.

The ordering is by **protectiveness**: `S0 < S1 < S2 < S3`. Combining evidence always takes
the maximum (the most protective tier), and a tier may only ever move *up* this order after a
scan (invariant I-8: tiers never decrease on revalidation).

oneOf.description:
Regenerable: a verified generated artifact, reproducible from tracked inputs.
Preselected for review, but never executed without confirmation.
Costly to recreate: reproducible, but needs a significant download or build. Opt-in.
Uncertain: ownership, activity or reproducibility is unclear. Never preselected.
Protected: possibly unique data, in active use, or explicitly protected. Never acted on.
